feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{ft}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=6{t}^{2}-4{t}^{3},$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-5\,\text{ft}/\text{s}$ when $t=2\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{ft/s}$) of the particle at time $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (6{t}^{2}-4{t}^{3})\text{d}t \\  & =2{t}^{3}-{t}^{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(2)=-5.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-5 & =2(2)^{3}-(2)^{4}+C \\ -5 & =16-16+C \\ C & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2{t}^{3}-{t}^{4}-5.$
